primary_topics: Address at the 13th Human Life International Asia Pacific Congress on Faith, Life and Family, October 8, 2006 -- 11 countries' delegates; 'family life is a subject close to my heart'

Constitutional and statutory framework for marriage and family: the Philippine Constitution's protections for marriage as an inviolable social institution; the Family Code's definition of marriage as a special contract of permanent union between a man and a woman
The Supreme Court's role in protecting marriage: strict scrutiny of annulment and nullity petitions; in case of doubt, affirmation of the marriage's validity
Family Courts (RA 8369, October 28, 1997): exclusive original jurisdiction over child and family cases; promoting child's and family's dignity, worth, and privacy
sub_topics: Constitutional framework: 'Our Constitution commands the State to protect marriage as an inviolable social institution and the foundation of the family... the State shall equally protect the life of the mother and the life of the unborn from conception. Notice that the protection is from conception, not from birth; that is why abortion is outlawed in our country.'

Family Code definition: 'marriage as a special contract of permanent union between a man and a woman, entered into in accordance with law, for the establishment of conjugal and family life. It is the foundation of the family and an inviolable social institution whose nature, consequences and incidents, are governed by law and are not subject to stipulation.'

SC strict scrutiny of annulments: 'the Court has consistently upheld the sanctity of marriage and the solidarity of the family by strictly scrutinizing proceedings for the annulment of marriage... In cases of doubt, it has affirmed the wedding's validity.'
Family Courts: Republic Act No. 8369 (October 28, 1997); exclusive original jurisdiction over child and family cases; promote child's and family's dignity and worth; respect their privacy

Global family challenges: changes in family structures, demographic aging, and rise of migration; test the family's 'ability to fulfill basic human functions of production, reproduction and socialization'

Closing: 'the union of a man and woman is the most enduring human institution -- honored and encouraged in all cultures and by every religious faith. Ages of experience have taught humanity that the commitment of a husband and wife to love and to serve each other promotes the welfare of children and the stability of society. This we can do by defending and strengthening the family, God's hope for humanity.'

stances.claim: The Philippine Constitution's protection of the unborn 'from conception, not from birth' is the constitutional basis for the absolute prohibition on abortion in the Philippines. This is a direct constitutional text argument, not a natural law or religious argument -- making it judicially unassailable as long as the Constitution is unchanged.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered October 8, 2006 at the 13th Human Life International Asia Pacific Congress -- 11 countries' delegates; 'family life is a subject close to my heart' -- this address by CJP presents the Philippine constitutional and statutory framework for protecting marriage and family. The Constitution: protect marriage as an inviolable social institution; recognize the sanctity of family life; support parents' primary right and duty in rearing youth; 'The State shall equally protect the life of the mother and the life of the unborn from conception. Notice that the protection is from conception, not from birth; that is why abortion is outlawed in our country.' The Family Code defines marriage as 'a special contract of permanent union between a man and a woman... for the establishment of conjugal and family life... an inviolable social institution whose nature, consequences and incidents, are governed by law and are not subject to stipulation.' The SC's governing judicial policy: 'consistently upheld the sanctity of marriage by strictly scrutinizing proceedings for the annulment of marriage... In cases of doubt, it has affirmed the wedding's validity.' Family Courts (RA 8369, October 28, 1997): exclusive original jurisdiction over child and family cases; advance family's dignity, worth and privacy. Global family challenges: changing family structures, demographic aging, migration. Closing: 'the union of a man and woman is the most enduring human institution -- honored and encouraged in all cultures and by every religious faith. Ages of experience have taught humanity that the commitment of a husband and wife to love and to serve each other promotes the welfare of children and the stability of society. This we can do by defending and strengthening the family, God's hope for humanity.'
